title: Pulling Carrots for Supper
description: Pull orange roots from a garden row and rinse the harvest for supper.
cardDescription: Pull orange roots from a garden row and rinse the harvest for supper.
focus: The setting is pulling Carrots for Supper. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Plant part taking up water below ground
Line of things side by side
Flat green part of a plant
Crackling sound when biting crisp food

answerNotes.CARROT: The part of a carrot usually eaten is its root. The leafy green top grows above the soil.
answerNotes.ROOT: Roots anchor a plant and take up water from the soil. They are below the stem, even when part of a root is visible above ground.
answerNotes.SOIL: Soil is the material around garden roots. It contains more than loose mineral particles: air, water, and decaying material are also part of it.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a line of things side by side. Garden plants, theater seats, and letters in a puzzle can all be arranged in rows.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.
answerNotes.FORK: A fork's prongs hold pieces of food. A garden fork is a larger tool sharing that pronged shape.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.TOP: A toy top spins on a point. Top can also mean the highest part of an object, so the action in the clue matters.
answerNotes.GREEN: Green describes many growing leaves. It is also a color name in its own right, so read whether the clue asks for a plant or its appearance.

words: Wire support placed around a tomato plant
Upright support for a garden plant

answerNotes.TOMATO: Tomatoes are used like vegetables in savory cooking. Botanically, their seed-bearing fruits belong in the fruit category.
answerNotes.RIPE: Ripe means ready to eat or harvest. Ripeness and color do not have exactly the same relationship in every kind of fruit.
answerNotes.JUICE: Juice is liquid released from fruit or vegetables. Pulp is the soft plant material that may remain mixed into it.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.PICK: Pick can mean choose or pluck. In a harvest setting, it usually means gathering something from the plant.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.

answerNotes.EAR: Ears receive sound. In an animal clue, the word usually asks for a body part rather than a call or other sound.
answerNotes.YELLOW: Yellow is a color name rather than a material. The movie's yellow brick road combines a color with a building block.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a line of things side by side. Garden plants, theater seats, and letters in a puzzle can all be arranged in rows.
answerNotes.SEED: A seed contains the beginning of a new plant. A seed packet's planting instructions describe how to help it start growing.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.

answerNotes.SOIL: Soil is the material around garden roots. It contains more than loose mineral particles: air, water, and decaying material are also part of it.
answerNotes.PEEL: Peel can name an outer covering or the action of removing it. Citrus rind and potato skin are familiar examples.
answerNotes.BAKE: Baking uses dry heat in an oven. Boiling instead cooks food in bubbling liquid.
